cost: ONE OF HIS OWN PINS WAS RELEASED, BY HIM, AND IT IS THE LOUDEST THING IN THIS ROUND. recal_110's `LAL '00 OFF rank <= 5` sat EXACTLY on 5 with zero slack. The round was measured, DECLINED on the conflict and reported; he ruled "Release the Lakers rank". The pin is now in data/anchors_superseded.json carrying that sentence verbatim, and is RE-PINNED at <= 6 for round 170 with recal_110's ruling text unchanged. Its SIBLING value pin — Lakers '00 best legal five, team:offdial 64 +-4 — is UNTOUCHED and reads 65 before and after, which is the reading his 2000 complaint ("How is this team 47 OFF with 2 all time great players") was actually about.

WHY THE PIN MOVED, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT THE LAKERS. Their five's offence is byte-identical at 126.426 raw: team offence is computed from ATTRIBUTES and this round moves none. Sam Perkins '00 (20.0 mpg, 3pt 88, volume 18 — the class the round corrects) falls OVR 59 -> 57; bestfive.ts picks by total OVR, so Indiana swaps him for Travis Best '00 and IND's offence rises 124.685 -> 126.891, passing them. VERIFIED BY SUBSTITUTION rather than inferred: base + Robert Horry '00 at 34 only -> 5 of 28, PASS; base + Perkins at OVR 59 -> PASS; at 58 (a TIE, which bestfive resolves against Perkins) -> FAIL; at 57 -> FAIL. The whole margin was one point of one card's OVR, and that card is not a Laker.

THE SUBJECT LANDS AT 60 AGAINST A STATED 55, AND THE FIVE POINTS ARE STRUCTURAL. Sam Hauser '23's STANDARD PATH already prints 55 — 55 is what he reads with the floor deleted outright — so NO positive share of a 13.68-point correction can reach it. His new anchor is therefore written at 60 +-3, with the reason on the pin. A later round that wants 55 is asking for the floor to be SWITCHED OFF below some minutes line, not scaled, and that is a different claim with a different constant. Marshall lands 53 against 52 and Bullard 54 against 52, both dead on.

THE THREE FORMS THAT WERE MEASURED, which is the cap the doctrine allows. (1) THE PRODUCT of the arc share and the load share, SHIPPED: Hauser 60, Marshall 53, Bullard 54. (2) THE GEOMETRIC MEAN of the two, recal_139's rule: Hauser 63 — rejected on its own terms as well as on the number, because r139's rule is for two readings of ONE claim and these are two different facts. (3) THE LOAD SHARE ON THE BIG BRANCH'S THREE ADDED TERMS ONLY (`0.17 x (orb + rim) + 0.10 x volume`), the literal hole recal_96 named: Hauser 61 — further from him, and it leaves the wing floor's own correction unpriced. recal_130's SECOND_FULL line was also read and rejected: this floor is a max() that REPLACES the standard path, not a second payment on top of it.

recal_96's NAMED HOLE IS NOW CLOSED, AND IT IS CLOSED ON THE CORRECTION RATHER THAN ON THE BAR. Its COST said "the big branch does carry a raw 0.10 * volume... it is the second place to look if a bench big reads high". That raw `0.10 * volume` is still there on purpose — scaling it alone reaches nobody — and what carries the load share now is the whole correction the floor makes to the standard path. The off-ball floor was the LAST claim in o_score that took no load share: recal_155's glue floor multiplies its gate by `_load`, recal_107's two-level premium and recal_163's interior term scale by SECOND_FULL, recal_151's rim-anchor premium blends on load_share, and the standard path's two load bars have been discounted since recal_96.

ONE TAX RE-RATIFIED, AND IT BROKE ALONE AND ON THE OTHER EDGE. crash def glass read blind -0.2483 at main's 0.38, over the -0.30 ceiling: the movers are low-minute STRETCH BIGS who crash the glass (Obi Toppin '25 66 -> 61 OVR, Matt Bonner '05, Channing Frye '16, Mike Muscala '17), so a class of rebounding fours thins out of the harness's ovr>=55 sample and the fives it draws rebound more ALIKE — which makes a blind crash call cost less. Swept ONCE from main's constants as the law requires: feasible 0.455 (blind -0.3006 exactly; 0.454 reads -0.2999 and fails) to 0.789 (oracle +0.5000 exactly at 0.790), a WIDE 0.334, true midpoint by r126's rule 0.38 -> 0.62 (blind -0.4166, oracle +0.5542). hunt HELD at 3.97 and crashOff at 0.08 — the first round in four where the two crash taxes did not break together — and the six others never moved. All nine pass.

THE ROUND NUMBER IS 170 AND THE PIPELINE VERSION IS LEFT AT 167. Per the doctrine of 2026-09-03 the constant stays where main had it and the integrator stamps the batch's highest round after ONE merged regeneration. data/build_ratings.py was not run and no attribute moved, so public/provenance.json is untouched.

ROUND 169 IS LANDING IN PARALLEL ON THE SIBLING FLOOR AND THE TWO ARE DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION. 169 gates recal_155's GLUE floor, which is `if not is_big(p) and a['volume'] < GL_V_HI` — a perimeter branch. This round's 259 movers are inside recal_64's `3pt`-gated branch and the overwhelming majority take recal_91's `is_big` half. Neither round touches the other's constants; the integrator can fold both.
notes: WHAT THE THREE SCOUT ITEMS SHARE. Sam Hauser '23: 16.1 mpg, 6.4 ppg, 14.7% usage, 3pt 99; standard path 59.43 of o_score against a floor of 73.11 that BINDS, so 13.68 points — a fifth of the card — were a correction paid in full for sixteen minutes of work. He read OFF 68, ten above Kyle Korver '15 (pinned 58 at 32.2 mpg on 49.2% from the arc) and six above Steve Kerr '96 (pinned 61). Donyell Marshall '07: 16.8 mpg, standard path 42.7 printed, floor 70.0, a printed lift of +22.4 — the largest stretch-big lift in the pool. Matt Bullard '92: 16.0 mpg, standard path 51.64, floor 70.83. 175 binding-floor cards are under twenty minutes and 19 of them read OFF 60 or better.

WHY THE SHARE GOES ON THE CORRECTION AND WHY IT IS A PRODUCT. recal_118 settled the first half: the floor is not a rival score but a CORRECTION to the standard path, so a share belongs on `(_fl - std)` and not on `_fl` — a scaled floor sinks below the standard path long before the share bites. This round adds the second half: recal_118's share answered ONE question, how much of a spacer the man is, and never asked how much of a game he played. Those are two different facts about two different things, so they multiply — a man who is only a third of a spacer AND only a third of a starter has earned a ninth of the correction, and that is the honest reading. Combining them by geometric mean (recal_139's rule for two readings of one claim) was measured and takes Hauser to 63.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool. 259 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN (a load share can only discount a correction; there are ZERO rises), max -12, mean -2.31. By minutes: 146 movers under 20 mpg (mean -2.88), 113 between 20 and 24 (mean -1.58), and ZERO at 24 or above — nothing at full load moves at all, which is the round's first requirement. DEF moves on ZERO cards, no attribute moves, and OVR follows on 178. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name.

THE CLASS IS FOUND BY THE TERM AND NOT BY A NAME. The largest movers are one archetype: Marshall '07 65 -> 53, Bullard '92 66 -> 54, Scott Padgett '02 64 -> 55, Doug McDermott '19 65 -> 56, Hauser '23 68 -> 60, Bullard '93 67 -> 59, Mike Muscala '17 60 -> 53, Channing Frye '16 62 -> 55, Duop Reath '24 64 -> 57, Vladimir Radmanović '09 62 -> 55, Matt Bonner '05 68 -> 62, Brian Cook '06 68 -> 64, Trey Lyles '18 67 -> 61, Obi Toppin '25 72 -> 65. Fifty-two of the 259 read OFF 60 or better before the round. Every one is a sub-twenty-minute shooting big who was priced as though he spaced the floor for thirty-six.
